fatal_errors: The proposed Q235 steel system does not reconstruct the target SS316L substrate with an atmospheric-plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating.
The intervention is low-temperature oxidation of bare steel rather than HEA coating deposition followed by 2 h annealing, especially at the target optimum of 550 °C.
The proposed 3.5 wt.% NaCl exposures at room temperature and 60 °C omit the target 3.5 wt.% H2SO4 electrochemical test and 900 °C cyclic Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 hot-corrosion environments.
The asserted formation of a protective Mn-rich oxide on Q235 steel at 300–350 °C is unsupported by cited prior evidence and is explicitly uncertain in terms of Mn transport and film stability.
explanation: The hypothesis is a coherent but largely unrelated corrosion study. It overlaps with the target only at a generic level: a surface oxide is proposed to inhibit chloride ingress, and lower corrosion current, higher impedance, and reduced mass loss are predicted relative to an untreated reference. It misses the target material, HEA coating, annealing series, BCC/FCC and grain-refinement mediators, Al/Cr-rich passive products, sulfuric-acid testing, and 900 °C molten-salt cycling. The proposed experiment is reasonably falsifiable because it combines XPS/SEM-EDS verification of the mediator with electrochemical and gravimetric outcomes, although annealing effects are not cleanly separated from Mn enrichment by an appropriate annealed control lacking Mn enrichment. With no supporting evidence and a questionable selective-Mn-oxidation premise, it cannot be considered a supported alternative or reconstruction.
